title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The notes generalise the profinite 'équation des lacets'. A profinite group 𝔊 is given with distinguished elements ρ, σ and an element τ (also written τ'), with 𝔊^+ an extension of 𝔊. The model is π̂1 of P^1 minus 3 points, or a triangle/modular-type quotient. The surrounding pages study Z_{ρ,σ}: automorphisms u of 𝔊^+ that preserve the conjugacy classes of the inertia-type subgroups L_ρ, L_σ, with a cyclotomic character χ and signs ε, ε'. S_0Γ_{ρ,σ} is the group of triples x=(u,a,b), where a, b are elements realising u(ρ), u(σ) as conjugates of powers of ρ, σ. S𝒢^#_{ρ,σ} is the set of solutions (α,β,μ) ∈ 𝔊×𝔊×Ẑ^* of the loop equation [α,ρ]=[β,σ]·ε_1^{μ-1}. (75)–(80) build an injection S_0Γ_{ρ,σ} ↪ S𝒢^#_{ρ,σ} via formula (76). Composing with S𝒢^# → Σ^# ≅ Z_{ρ,σ} gives the projection (u,a,b) ↦ u, which is surjective.

Step 1 (this page, (82)–(84)). Fix the signs ε=(-1)^ν, ε'=(-1)^{ν'}. The free right action (81) of (a_0,b_0) ∈ SN*_ρ×SN*_σ on S𝒢 is (α,β,μ) ↦ (αa_0, βb_0, μ). Through (76) it corresponds on S_0Γ to (83): (u,a,b) ↦ (u, τ^{ν'}(a_0^{-1})a, τ^{ν}(b_0^{-1})b). That is left translation by (τ^{ν'},τ^ν)·(a_0,b_0)^{-1}, so it is again free and fibrewise transitive over Z_{ρ,σ}. The injection (79) is an equivariant map between torsors over the same base under compatible groups, and it covers a surjection on the bases. It is therefore surjective, which gives the isomorphism (84): S_0Γ_{ρ,σ} ≅ S𝒢^#_{ρ,σ}.

Step 2 ((85)–(86)). Left translation by ℓ ∈ L_0 inside S_0Γ_{ρ,σ} becomes (α,β,μ) ↦ (ℓα, ℓβ, μ), which visibly preserves the solution set. Passing to the quotient gives (86): Γ_{ρ,σ} ≅ L_0\S𝒢^#_{ρ,σ}. So the 'outer' group Γ_{ρ,σ} is described as orbits of solutions of the loop equation.

Step 3 ((87)). There is an enlarged version S_0M_{ρ,σ}, with quadruples x=(u,a,b,𝒰), where 𝒰 is a further datum compatible with u (an element/automorphism of 𝔊^+). It maps bijectively to S𝒢^#_{ρ,σ}×𝔊^+ by α = u a^{-1} τ^{ν'_ρ(a)}, β = u b^{-1} τ^{ν_σ(b)}, μ = χ(x), f = u𝒰^{-1}. Here μ is the common value of the characters of u, a, b, 𝒰. Bijectivity is said to be trivial from (84).

Purpose. This is the abstract, Drinfeld–Ihara-style parametrisation of a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group of 'admissible' automorphisms by solutions of a loop equation. It is done for a general profinite group with two distinguished 'inertia' elements, not only F̂_2. The next page begins functoriality under surjections 𝔊 → 𝔊'.
errors: No genuine mathematical error is visible. The argument 'injective equivariant map of torsors over a surjection is bijective' is sound, provided the actions are free and transitive on fibres; (81) and the previous page assert this.
Notation is inconsistent: (83) uses τ^{ν'}, τ^ν, while (87) uses τ'^{ν'_ρ(a)} and τ'^{ν_σ(b)}. The same element τ = τ' is presumably meant.

The meaning of 'τ^{ν'}(a_0^{-1})' (conjugation by τ^{ν'} versus a product) is not specified on this page. The rewriting as 'translation à gauche par (τ^{ν'},τ^ν)(a_0,b_0)^{-1}' only makes sense if it denotes the product τ^{ν'}·a_0^{-1}, or if conjugation is meant inside a semidirect product.

ideas.what: Description of the group of inertia-preserving automorphisms (rigidified) as the solution set of a loop equation [α,ρ]=[β,σ]ε^{μ-1} in 𝔊×𝔊×Ẑ^*
ideas.modern_name: Drinfeld/Ihara-type parametrisation of (profinite) Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type groups by pairs (λ,f) satisfying relations; generalised GT for triangle-type groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1980s–1990); Lochak–Schneps and others for variants
ideas.where_published: The idea of an 'équation des lacets' is announced in La Longue Marche (1981, circulated) and alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme. This detailed form is unpublished.

ideas.what: Bijectivity via an equivariant injection of torsors over a surjective base map
Outer group Γ_{ρ,σ} ≅ L_0\S𝒢^#: quotient of the solution set by a diagonal left action
ideas.modern_name: passing from Aut to Out (rigidification modulo inner/inertia)

ideas.what: Enlarged parametrisation S_0M_{ρ,σ} ≅ S𝒢^# × 𝔊^+ adding the free parameter f = u𝒰^{-1}

missed.claim: The page completes, in full detail, an abstract version of the loop-equation description of an automorphism group, Γ ≅ L_0\{solutions of [α,ρ]=[β,σ]ε^{μ-1}}. It does so for an arbitrary profinite group with two distinguished inertia elements, not only F̂_2. This general framework, together with the functoriality the next page develops, is a pre-Drinfeld, pre-Lochak–Schneps treatment that is not in the published record. The page itself is only a routine verification step within it.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's own general formalism for GT-type groups attached to arbitrary profinite 'triangle' data. That formalism is relevant to historical attribution and to later generalisations, such as GT-actions on quotients of F̂_2 and triangle groups.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a technical step (surjectivity and the quotient isomorphism) inside a larger, historically interesting but already known-in-spirit programme: Grothendieck's loop equation as a precursor of GT. Nothing new beyond that framework appears on this page.
transcription_corrections: The superscript written 'ff' on S𝒢 is the sharp sign: S𝒢^#_{ρ,σ}, consistent with the previous page.
In (87) the parenthetical chain of characters probably reads χ_Z(u)=χ_ρ(a)=χ_σ(b)=χ_𝔊(𝒰), not χ_2(u) and χ_𝒰(𝒰).
The ambient set in (87) is written ∈ 𝔊×𝔊×Ẑ^*×𝔊^+ (Ẑ^* rather than Ẑ_1^×).
(85) reads (ℓα, ℓβ, μ) with ℓ ∈ L_0; the struck-out phrase is 'dont il était clair a priori qu'elles stabilisent'.
